newsitem.title: FRANCE: France confirms some company tax may apply to 1996.
newsitem.headline: France confirms some company tax may apply to 1996.

text.p: The French Finance Ministry on Monday confirmed that the increase in corporation tax, announced last week, would also apply to some earnings made in 1996 by companies whose fiscal year does not end on December 31.

"Because of tax equality, all companies with sales over 50 million francs ($8.1 million) have to pay the 15 percent increase if they have made profits during the year 1997," a ministry spokeswoman said.
The government last week introduced a 15 percent surcharge on corporate taxes for 1997 and 1998, bringing the tax rate for these two years to 41.6 percent from 36.6 percent.
The tax rise will also apply to units of foreign companies having sales in France of over 50 million francs.
"It's the same solution as has been applied when the first 10 percent surcharge was introduced by the Juppe government in 1995," the Finance Ministry spokeswoman said.
"It's impossible to do it differently because that would mean we would tax companies at different rates depending whether their year ends at December 31, 1997 or before that date," she said.
The spokeswoman said that a company with a fiscal year ending on March 31, 1997 would be taxed at the higher rate for the period April 1, 1996 to March 31.
